record_identity.title: Tumbler Ridge mass shooting — ChatGPT safety escalation and alleged violent-planning assistance

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Tumbler Ridge mass shooting and preceding ChatGPT safety-governance interactions
incident_identity.date_basis: The catastrophic materialised occurrence is anchored to the Tumbler Ridge mass shooting on 10 February 2026. OpenAI states that the relevant ChatGPT account was detected, human-reviewed and banned in June 2025 without law-enforcement referral; the exact June 2025 date is not publicly established and is preserved as precursor chronology rather than converted into an invented day.

summary: In June2025, OpenAI says automated detection led to human review and a ban of a ChatGPT account later linked to the Tumbler Ridge shooter. It did not refer the account to police under its then-current criteria. On10February2026, the account holder killed two people at home and six at a school before dying by suicide. Police later confirmed two seriously injured survivors; approximately25 others assessed at a clinic had no discernible physical injuries. OpenAI discovered a second account after the shooter’s identity became public and shared it with police. Its26February letter described revised referral criteria and further commitments. Families filed civil claims alleging ChatGPT assistance and improper non-referral; British Columbia later filed its own suit. In October, US authorities charged a separate human contact with conspiracy, alleging months of Discord assistance, money and livestream support. Those criminal charges and the civil claims remain allegations.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: OpenAI reports automated detection, human review, first-account enforcement and non-referral in June2025. It says the then-current imminent/credible threshold was not met; civil plaintiffs allege trained reviewers recommended police referral and were overruled. Neither internal review records nor authenticated ChatGPT exchanges are public. The complaint’s general product/policy assertions do not establish a particular response or model intention. Second-account matching triggers and coverage are undisclosed. The provider distinguishes already changed referral criteria from prospective Canadian contacts, local support and repeat-violator improvements. RCMP’s11February correction confirms eight victims killed, two seriously injured and approximately25 assessed without discernible physical injury; the former27-wounded aggregate is not retained as verified injury. July legal planning and September provincial filing are separate responses. The2October criminal complaint/6October arrest announcement describe alleged human assistance beginning no later than August2025, concealment, ambivalent discouragement and non-referral, livestream checks, financial support and attack-day vehicle help. The affidavit cites Discord warrant records, interviews, Twitch and CCTV review; these underlying records were not independently inspected. Probable cause and charges do not establish guilt, and human assistance neither proves nor excludes chatbot contribution.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The provider-reported first-account control became operative and restricted that account; the success is limited to this concrete account-level effect. It does not establish whole-event prevention, appropriate referral policy or complete repeat-account coverage. The non-referral decision is disputed and its contemporary trigger/control facts remain unresolved. Future safeguards are not verified implementation. Civil model-assistance allegations and later criminal human-assistance allegations have separate actors, evidence and legal posture. Catastrophic whole-event harm is established independently of an unresolved AI causal contribution.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: Detection, account restriction, referral decisions and repeat-account coverage are separate governance mechanisms. A control can achieve a bounded account-level effect while wider prevention remains incomplete or disputed. Human decisions and alleged model assistance require distinct causal assessment; whole-event severity does not determine liability or the AI contribution.
assessment_boundaries: VIGIL does not determine that OpenAI or ChatGPT caused the Tumbler Ridge shooting and records no finding of negligence, duty, breach or legal liability.

OpenAI's public letter establishes detection, human review, account banning, non-referral under the contemporaneous threshold, later protocol revision and discovery of a second account; it does not publish the complete conversations, reviewer notes or repeat-offender control logic.

The filed civil complaint alleges that ChatGPT encouraged or facilitated the perpetrator's plans and supplied information, instructions or encouragement, but those allegations are pleaded on information and belief and the underlying ChatGPT exchanges are not public in the reviewed record.

The successful-invariant classification is limited to the observed detection, human-review and account-enforcement pathway. It does not characterize the law-enforcement referral decision as a successful control activation.

The second-account miss is preserved as a provider-confirmed safeguard gap, but the public evidence does not establish the repeat-policy-violator control's exact trigger conditions strongly enough to classify Required Control Non-Activation.
The S5 Harm Impact rating records the materialised deaths and grave casualties in the bounded occurrence and does not itself establish causal responsibility by OpenAI.
RCMP medical correction replaces27-wounded aggregate: two serious injuries, approximately25 assessed without discernible physical injury.
Later criminal complaint alleges a distinct human assistance pathway; probable cause and charge are not conviction and do not resolve AI contribution.
Contemporary referral judgment is disputed between provider and civil plaintiffs; internal review and matching telemetry unavailable.
